title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: Datadog
providers.scope_notes: IP documentation differs on entitlement (Pro+ via support vs Enterprise). Confirm contract. AWS WIF requires supported integration/configuration.

controls.name: IP Allowlist
controls.what: Blocks UI, public API and OAuth app access from IPs outside the list; Agent intake and some endpoints are exempt.
controls.setting: Organization Settings > Security > IP Allowlist; IP Allowlist API; Terraform ip_allowlist (Org Management permission)
controls.plan: Pro+ or Enterprise, enabled via support (API reference says Enterprise)
controls.quote: When the IP allowlist is enabled, only IP addresses or CIDR ranges in the allowlist can access the Datadog API and UI.

controls.name: Disable OAuth access for an application
controls.what: Turns off an OAuth app and revokes it for all users in the org.
controls.setting: Organization Settings > OAuth Apps (Admin role or org_authorized_apps_read/write)
controls.quote: Disabling OAuth access for an application revokes access to this application for all users in your organization.

controls.name: Revoke a user's OAuth access
controls.what: Removes one user's authorization for an OAuth app; the user can re-authorize.
controls.quote: Revoking a user's OAuth access to an application removes all access to that application.

controls_unknown: No org setting found that blocks personal application keys or forces service-account-only keys.

Whether the IP allowlist applies to API-key and client-token requests outside telemetry intake is not stated; entitlement differs between account docs (Pro+/Enterprise) and API reference (Enterprise).
Plan requirement for Agent-based WIF: current WIF page lists no tier; earlier material says Enterprise-only and preview.
How to delete or disable an identity mapping is not documented on the WIF page; intake mappings are deleted via API.
Whether custom roles (needed to narrow these permissions) require a specific plan was not confirmed.

authentication.summary: Organization API key, often combined with a user/service-account application key; OAuth for supported apps; workload federation for supported scenarios.

federation.details: OAuth authorization-code grant with PKCE and user consent. No external identity/assertion exchange is documented for this path; AWS workload federation is a separate path (datadog-3).

ip_restriction.boundary: Org IP allowlist explicitly covers third-party apps accessing Datadog through OAuth. Org-wide only; cannot be scoped to a token, key, user or endpoint.

renewal.summary: Refresh token obtains a new 1-hour access token. Marketplace OAuth client refresh tokens have no expiration until the user revokes authorization; other client types not stated.

administration.summary: Application-key scopes, service accounts, role permissions, OAuth grants, IP allowlist and key revocation.
administration.conditions: IP documentation differs on entitlement (Pro+ via support vs Enterprise). Confirm contract. AWS WIF requires supported integration/configuration.

inventory.details: Organization Settings > Mobile and Third-Party Access lists OAuth apps and the users who authorized each one.

expiry.api: Fixed 1-hour access token TTL, returned by POST /api/v2/oauth2/token; not configurable

usage.ui: Audit Trail explorer; filter by Authentication Attributes facets

log_sources.name: Datadog Audit Trail
log_sources.notes: Request events for API calls plus product events; records @auth_method and key IDs. Default 90-day retention when enabled (3-90 days); 7 days when disabled.

credential_id_fields.notes: OAuth client used when @auth_method is oauth_token
OAuth client asset on oauth_client events

anomaly_cues: OAuth client name not on the approved app list
OAuth token use by a user who was deactivated or lost the role

containment.steps: Revoke tokens via POST /oauth2/v1/revoke or user revokes app authorization; delete the OAuth client.
containment.notes: Refresh tokens never expire until revoked; access tokens last 1 hour. Not documented whether revoking a refresh token kills issued access tokens.
